method: Independent first-pass scoring against each item's explicit gold checks. Automated rule-assisted checklist; not blind human adjudication. Exact totals are directional and sensitive to checklist interpretation.
score_scale: Each matched check contributes equally; normalized to 10 points per item.
important_observations: Near-identical aggregate scores and 44 of 50 paired ties: no meaningful overall quality separation is established by this one 50-item authored set.
Both models followed the deterministic arithmetic, box-logic, JSON/CSV, and most constrained-format prompts accurately in this run.
I09 word-count limit: both outputs appear over the requested 180-230 words even with max effort and 2000 output-token cap; effort did not cure this instruction-following weakness.

I07: GPT-6 response more directly stated the evidence gap and marked the plan as not yet performed; GPT-5.6 gave a more expansive source plan but included an unsupported stronger statement that the summary cannot confirm the claims.

I13: GPT-6 chose None for empty input and preserved normal behavior; GPT-5.6 chose ValueError. Both stated an explicit contract and valid tests, so this is a contract choice rather than a correctness distinction.

I29/I30: GPT-5.6 more fully described uncertainty and decision context; one I30 response suggested sample-size calculations without showing a verified calculation, so treat numeric recommendation cautiously.
I37: both communicated known incident facts without asserting the absence of a breach; GPT-5.6 included a continuing-update commitment.
I49: both proposed measurable criteria and explicitly labeled the numbers as proposals, not existing service-level facts.
limitations: One generation per item; this is not a variance estimate or statistically powered benchmark.
Prompts were authored for this comparison and scoring was not blinded; subjective writing tasks and heuristic checks carry evaluator bias.
Cost and latency are one gateway run and may vary with load, cache and upstream routing.
The suite disables external tools; it evaluates response capability, not full tool-using agent performance.
The earlier low/default-effort run is not strictly comparable because reasoning effort and output-token budget differ.
